verses.sanskrit: नारद उवाच।  पृथुं वैन्यं च राजानं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम।  यमभ्यषिञ्चन् साम्राज्ये राजसूये महर्षयः ॥१॥
verses.english: Narada said We heard also, O Srinjaya, that Vena's son Prithu, who was installed as the emperor of the world by the mighty sages on the celebration of his Rajasuya-sacrifice, had also to suffer death.

verses.sanskrit: यत्नतः प्रथितेत्यूचुः सर्वानभिभवन् पृथुः।  क्षतान्नस्त्रास्यते सर्वानित्येवं क्षत्त्रियोऽभवत् ॥२॥
verses.english: Having vanquished all his foes with great efforts, he consolidated his empire, for which he came to be called Prithu (or the celebrated). He became a true Kshatriya, owing to his protecting his subjects from wounds and injuries.

verses.sanskrit: पृथुं वैन्यं प्रजा दृष्ट्वा रक्ताः स्मेति यदब्रुवन्।  ततो राजेति नामास्य अनुरागाद‌जायत ॥३॥
अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी आसीद्वैन्यस्य कामधुक्। सर्वाः कामदुघा गावः पुटके पुटके मधु ॥४॥
verses.english: The Earth yielded corn without being cultivated and for Vena's son Prithu she fulfilled all his desires. The cows also yielded milk whenever desired and every lotus-bud was filled with honey.

verses.sanskrit: आसन् हिरण्मया दर्भाः सुखस्पर्शाः सुखावहाः। तेषां चीराणि संवीताः प्रजास्तेष्वेव शेरते ॥५॥
verses.english: The sacred Kusha grass were all made of gold and were delicate to the touch and otherwise delightful. The people used to wear cloths made of this grass and they used to lie down on beds composed of them.

verses.sanskrit: फलान्यमृतकल्पानि स्वादूनि च मधूनि च।  तेषामासीत्तदाहारो निराहाराश्च नाभवन् ॥६॥
verses.english: Fruits, nectareous, tasteful and delicate, then became their chief edible; and none went without food.
verses.bhavadeepa: तेषां दर्भाणामेव चीराणि वल्कलानि यैः प्रजाः संवीताः तान्येव परिधानीयानि शयनानि चेत्यर्थः॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्था मनुष्या ह्यकुतोभयाः। न्यवसन्त यथाकामं वृक्षेषु च गुहासु च ॥७॥
प्रविभागो न राष्ट्राणां पुराणां चाभवत्तदा।  यथासुखं यथाकामं तथैता मुदिताः प्रजाः ॥८॥
verses.english: His dominions and his cities were not divided into smaller sections and countries. There his subjects lived delightedly, as it suited their desire or convenience.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य संस्तम्भिता ह्यापः समुद्रमभियास्यतः। पर्वताश्च ददुर्मार्गं ध्वजभङ्गश्च नाभवत् ॥९॥
तं वनस्पतयः शैला देवासुरनरोरगाः।  सप्तर्षयः पुण्यजना गन्धर्वाप्सरसोऽपि च ॥१०॥
पितरश्च सुखासीनमभिगम्येदमब्रुवन्।  सम्राडसिक्षत्रियोऽसि राजा गोप्ता पितासि नः ॥११॥
verses.english: Him seated at his ease, the mighty trees of the forest, the gods of the mountains, the celestials, the Asuras, the men and the replies the seven sages, sages, the holy ascetics, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras and the ancestral manes, approaching said these words-"You are our Emperor, you protect us from injuries, you are ever our delighter, saviour and father. Give us, O mighty monarch, O Master, the boons we desire to have-boons through whose virtue we may live in happiness and plenty, for eternal years.

verses.sanskrit: देह्यस्मभ्यं महाराज प्रभुः सन्नीप्सितान् वरान्।  यैर्वयं शाश्वतीस्तृप्तीर्वर्तयिष्यामहे सुखम् ॥१२॥
तथेत्युक्त्वा पृथुर्वैन्यो गृहीत्वाऽऽजगवं धनुः।  शरांश्चाप्रतिमान् घोरांश्चिन्तयित्वाऽब्रवीन्महीम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then saying yea' to all their prayers, Vena's son Prithu took up his Ajagava bow and several dreadful arrows, whose equals existed not; then thinking for a while, he

verses.sanskrit: एह्येहि वसुधे क्षिप्रं क्षरैभ्यः कांक्षितं पयः।  ततो दास्यामि भद्रं ते अन्नं यस्य यथेप्सितम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: "Come, come, O Earth, quickly give these my subjects the milk they desire. Good betide you; from the milk you shall shed, I desire to give my subjects the edibles they wish to have.

verses.sanskrit: वसुधोवाच। दुहितृत्वेन मां वीर सङ्कल्पयितुमर्हसि।  तथेत्युक्त्वा पृथुः सर्वं विधानमकरोद्वशी ॥१५॥
verses.english: The Earth said "O Hero, it behoves you to look upon me as your own daughter." Saying, “So be it” the self-controlled Prithu, then arranged for (milking the Earth).

verses.sanskrit: ततो भूतनिकायास्तां वसुधां दुदुहुस्तदा। तां वनस्पतयः पूर्वं समुत्तस्थुर्दुधुक्षवः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Then the whole assemblage of creatures begin to milk the Earth (successively). The mighty trees of the forest then first approached her, desirous of milking her.

verses.sanskrit: साऽतिष्ठद्वत्सला वत्सं दोग्धृपात्राणि चेच्छती। वत्सोऽभूत् पुष्पितः शालः प्लक्षो दोग्धाऽभवत् तदा ॥१७॥
verses.english: There then stood the highly affectionate Earth (as a cow), looking for a calf, a milker and a pot wherein to keep the milk. Then the flowering Shala tree became the calf and the Plaksha became the milker.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नप्ररोहणं दुग्धं पात्रमौदुम्बरं शुभम्।  उदयः पर्वतो वत्सो मेरुर्दोग्धा महागिरिः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Torn buds become the milk and the auspicious fig tree became the milk-pot. (Next the mountains appeared to milk her) The Eastern hill then became the calf and the mighty Meru-mountain became the milkman.

verses.sanskrit: रत्नान्योषधयो दुग्धं पात्रमश्ममयं तथा। दोग्धा चासीत्तदा देवो दुग्धमूर्जस्करं प्रियम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Jewels and precious stones and the Osadhis became the milk and the stones became the milk-jar. Next the celestials became the milkers and everything capable of imparting energy became the milk.

verses.sanskrit: असुरा दुदुहुर्मायामामपात्रे तु ते तदा।  दोग्धा द्विमूर्धा तत्रासीद्वत्सश्चासीद्विरोचनः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Next the Asuras milked urine from the Earth, in unbaked earthen jars. Dvimurdha (the two-headed) then became the milker and Virochana became the calf.
verses.bhavadeepa: दोग्धेति । चाद्वत्सोऽपि देव एव । प्रियं दुग्धं पात्रमप्यर्थान्मन एवेति कल्प्यम् । ग्रन्थान्तराद्वा वत्सपात्रे ज्ञेये । एवमन्यत्रापि ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: कृषिं च सस्यं च नरा दुदुहुः पृथिवीतले।  स्वायंभुवो मनुर्वत्सस्तेषां दोग्धाऽभवत् पृथुः ॥२१॥
अलाबुपात्रे च तथा विषं दुग्धा वसुन्धरा।  धृतराष्ट्रोऽभवद्दोग्धा तेषां वत्सस्तु तक्षकः ॥२२॥
सप्तर्षिभिर्ब्रह्म दुग्धा तथा चाक्लिष्टकर्मभिः। दोग्धा बृहस्पतिः पात्रं छन्दो वत्सश्च सोमराट् ॥२३॥
अन्तर्धानं चामपात्रे दुग्धा पुण्यजनैर्विराट्। दोग्धा वैश्रवणस्तेषां वत्सश्चासीद्वृषध्वजः ॥२४॥
verses.english: The Rakshasas milking her, in a jar of unbaked Earth, obtained the power of disappearing at will. Their milker Vaishravana and Vrishadhvaja was their calf.

verses.sanskrit: पुण्यगन्धान् पद्मपात्रे गन्धर्वाप्सरसोऽदुहन्। वत्सश्चित्ररथस्तेषां दोग्धा विश्वरुचिः प्रभुः ॥२५॥
verses.english: The Apsaras and the Gandharvas milked her of holy fragrance and received it in lotuspetals. Chitraratha became their calf and the lord Visvaruchi became their milker.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधां रजतपात्रेषु दुदुहुः पितरश्च ताम्।  वत्सो वैवस्वतस्तेषां यमो दोग्धाऽन्तकस्तदा ॥२६॥
verses.english: The ancestral manes milked her of Svadhas in pots of silver. Vaivasvata became their calf and the Destroyer (Yama) himself became their milker.

verses.sanskrit: एवं निकायैस्तैर्दुग्धा पयोऽभीष्टं हि सा विराट्।  यैर्वर्तयन्ति ते ह्यद्य पात्रैर्वत्सैश्च नित्यशः ॥२७॥
यज्ञैश्च विविधैरिष्ट्वा पृथुवैन्यः प्रतापवान्।  सन्तर्पयित्वा भूतानि सर्वैः कामैर्मनःप्रियैः ॥२८॥
हैरण्यानकरोद्राजा ये केचित् पार्थिवा भुवि। तान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रायच्छदश्वमेधे महामखे ॥२९॥
verses.english: The king caused all objects obtaining of the face of the Earth to be made of gold and on the occasion of his great Horse-sacrifice, he gave them away to the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: षष्टिनागसहस्राणि षष्टिनागशतानि च। सौवर्णानकरोद्राजा ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च तान् ददौ ॥३०॥
verses.english: The king caused sixty-six thousands images of elephants to be made of gold and he gave them away to the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: इमां च पृथिवीं सर्वां मणिरत्नविभूषिताम्। सौवर्णीमकरोद्राजा ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च तां ददौ॥३१॥
verses.english: The entire Earth adorned with jewels and gems, the king caused to be covered over with gold and he then gave her away to the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया।  पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः ॥३२॥
अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभिश्वैत्येति व्याहरन् ॥३३॥
verses.english: When even such a king, O Srinjaya, died, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and consequently far superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying-'O Shvaitya’, who did perform no sacrifice and make no sacrificial presents.
